basis: The document's own printed instructions, page 2 of the pinned binary (form INST MC 227a, Rev. 7/24), plus the printed text of page 1. Each entry cites the page and the measured baseline of the line it rests on. This step does not depend on the field map and was recorded from the same pinned bytes.

venue.value: The court in which the conviction occurred. A separate application is required for each court.

citation.text: You must file the application in the court where the conviction occurred. You must use a separate application for each court.

venue.note: This is why the family's boundary listing is still one filing: four convictions in one court go on one application; convictions in different courts do not.

filingMethod.value: In person at the clerk's office of the convicting court, with three copies of the application and all attachments.

citation.text: Make three copies of all attachments and this application. Take all copies to the court clerk for the court where you were convicted.

filingMethod.note: The document describes taking the copies to the clerk. It does not authorise mail or e-filing of the application itself, and this record does not add either.

filingFee.value: No filing fee for the application.

citation.text: There should be no filing fee for filing the application.

filingFee.discharges: The build worklist carried the caution "Confirm against the current MC 227a form and with MSP before quoting $0". The form side of that caution is now answered from the current pinned edition, REV-2024-07, in the document's own words. The Michigan State Police side is NOT answered here — this document says nothing about MSP fees — and remains open.

feeWaiverTreatment.value: Not applicable to the application itself, which carries no filing fee. A cost does arise for the certified copies the application must attach.

citation.text: There may be a fee to obtain these certified copies.

feeWaiverTreatment.note: A fee waiver record for the certified copies is a separate question this document does not answer.

requiredParticipantAttachments.value: A certified copy of EACH conviction listed, obtained from the clerk of the convicting court.

citations.text: Find out the exact date of each conviction and each charge from the court. Get a certified copy of each conviction from the clerk of the court in which you were convicted and attach it to your application.
2. A certified copy of each conviction is attached.

requiredParticipantAttachments.note: Per conviction, not per application: a four-conviction listing attaches four certified copies. The instruction also tells the participant to get the exact conviction date and charge FROM THE COURT — which is the document's own answer to why this family leaves the listing for them.

serviceRecipients.value: The office of the prosecuting official that prosecuted the offence(s).

citation.text: Mail a copy of the application packet to the office of the prosecuting official that prosecuted the offense(s).

serviceRecipients.note: The prosecuting official who prosecuted the offence, not the Attorney General.

serviceMethod.value: First-class mail to the last-known address as defined by MCR 2.107(C)(3).

citation.text: I served a copy of this application and certified record of conviction(s) on the prosecuting official by first-class mail addressed to their last-known address as defined by MCR 2.107(C)(3).

serviceMethod.servedDocuments: The application AND the certified record of conviction(s) — the certificate's own words.

serviceTiming.value: The packet is mailed to the prosecuting official BEFORE the Certificate of Mailing is completed and the court copy filed.

citation.text: On both remaining copies of the application, fill in the Certificate of Mailing. After you fill out and sign the Certificate of Mailing, mail or take one of the remaining application packets with the completed Certificate of Mailing to the court. Keep the other copy of the application packet for your records.

serviceTiming.consequenceForThisFamily: This is the document's own statement of why `comdate` and `comsig` are never prefilled: the certificate is completed after an act of mailing that has not happened at render time, and it is made under penalty of perjury in the form's printed words.

certificateOfService.value: Carried on page 1 of MC 227a itself, headed CERTIFICATE OF MAILING, sworn under penalty of perjury. Completed by the participant after mailing; never prefilled.

filingDeadline.note: MC 227a states no deadline for filing the application. The timing constraint on this route is the eligibility waiting period, which is an eligibility question and is not this family's to state.

uncontestedHearingTreatment.value: No hearing. If the prosecuting agency files no answer within 60 days of the date of service, the court enters an order and mails copies out.

citation.text: If no answer is filed by the prosecuting agency within 60 days of the date of service of the application, the court will enter an order and mail a copy to you, the arresting agency, the prosecuting agency, and the Michigan State Police.

uncontestedHearingTreatment.discrepancyToResolve: The route's own coded note in the build worklist says "absent an answer the court must enter the set-aside order within 21 days". The document does not state a 21-day figure. That number is not contradicted here and is not adopted here: it is flagged for counsel, because a coded claim and the official form disagreeing about a period is exactly the state-pack fidelity question the sprint's source hierarchy exists to catch.

contestedHearingOrOppositionHandoff.value: If the prosecuting agency opposes, the court must set a hearing within 30 days and mail notice; the applicant should appear.

citation.text: If the prosecuting agency files a response opposing your application, the court must set the matter for a hearing within 30 days and mail a copy of a notice of the hearing to you. You should appear in court on the date and time set by the court.

postFilingInstructions.value: Keep one complete copy of the application packet for the applicant's own records; the court mails the order to the applicant, the arresting agency, the prosecuting agency and the Michigan State Police.

citations.text: Keep the other copy of the application packet for your records.
the court will enter an order and mail a copy to you, the arresting agency, the prosecuting agency, and the Michigan State Police.

deliveryAndDistribution.value: The form's own distribution list: SRA, Court, Defendant, Prosecuting official, Return.

citation.text: Approved, SCAO — Distribute form to: SRA / Court / Defendant / Prosecuting official / Return

deliveryAndDistribution.note: Three copies plus the original, matching instruction 6's 'make three copies'.

schedulesOrContinuationPages.value: Additional sheets, at the applicant's discretion, when more than four convictions are listed.

citation.text: 1. I request that the court issue an order to set aside the following misdemeanor marihuana conviction(s)* as provided by law. Use additional sheet(s) if more space is necessary.

schedulesOrContinuationPages.note: The printed listing holds exactly four rows, a through d. The form provides no continuation form; it authorises a free-form additional sheet. A fifth conviction therefore has no mapped write box and never will have one on this document.

proposedOrder.note: MC 227a is the application only. The court enters its own order — page 2 says the court "will enter an order and mail a copy" — so this family drafts none. Whether a separate SCAO order form should be carried alongside is an open question this family does not answer, and no form number is asserted here that has not been bound by hash.

coverSheet.note: No cover sheet is named by MC 227a or its instructions.

notice.note: The notice of hearing is issued and mailed BY THE COURT, per page 2. It is not a participant deliverable.

affidavitOrVerification.note: No separate affidavit. The Certificate of Mailing is sworn under penalty of perjury, and notarisation is not required — consistent with the route record's "Not required by MCL 780.621e."

eligibilityStatutesPrintedOnTheDocument.recordedAsSourceNotAsAuthority: Transcribed from the document because a filer reads them off this page; this family creates no eligibility rule and changes none. Legal eligibility is outside this family's owned path.
value: Violation of a local ordinance substantially corresponding to one of the above

citation.text: 1. Determine whether you are eligible ... pursuant to MCL 780.621e. Eligible convictions include violation of the following:

value: Human-trafficking-related set-aside under MCL 780.621(3) uses form MC 227b, not this form.
A non-marihuana misdemeanor set-aside under MCL 780.621 uses form MC 227, not this form.

citations.text: Use note: If you are asking to have an eligible conviction set aside under MCL 780.621(3) because the offense committed was a direct result of you being a victim of human trafficking, you must use form MC 227b.
If you are asking to have a non-marihuana related misdemeanor conviction set aside under MCL 780.621, you must use form MC 227.

formSelectionWarningsPrintedOnTheDocumen.consequenceForRouting: This family's document is correct ONLY for misdemeanour marihuana convictions. Routing a trafficking-related or non-marihuana matter here would deliver the wrong form. Recorded as a constraint on the route that already exists; no route identity is created or changed here.

whatThisRecordDoesNotEstablish: that MC 227a REV-2024-07 is the current official edition
that the Michigan State Police charge nothing for their part of the process
that the 21-day figure in the route's coded note is wrong — only that this document does not state it
any eligibility determination for any participant
